Senator Rick Scott visits Israel to reaffirm U.S.-Israel partnership and security cooperation
Senator Rick Scott visited Israel for meetings focused on strengthening U.S.-Israel cooperation across defense initiatives. The visit included discussions with military officials about regional security concerns following recent attacks.
U.S. Senator Rick Scott visited Israel to reinforce the United States’ commitment to its alliance with Israel, according to an Oct. 21 announcement. Scott, a member of the Senate Armed Services and Foreign Relations committees, met with Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Sa’ar, members of the Israeli Defense Forces, U.S. servicemen and women, and Department of War personnel in Jerusalem.
During his visit, Scott discussed ongoing U.S.-Israeli collaboration on projects including efforts related to securing the U.S. southern border. He also traveled to the Golan Heights and Israel’s Northern Command, where he received briefings from both U.S. and Israeli military officials about operations in southern Lebanon.
Scott met with Dolan Abu Saleh, Mayor of Majdal Shams, as well as bereaved families from the Druze community who lost children during a Hezbollah attack on a soccer field in July 2024 that resulted in twelve deaths.
"From business partnerships to healthcare and medicine production, to defense technology, America’s partnership with Israel is the model of how America First alliances should operate," said Senator Rick Scott. "Too many people in America have lost sight of the fact that Israel is the good guy and that Qatar, Iran, including its proxies Hamas and Hezbollah, are the bad guys who indiscriminately target and murder innocent people. Israel faces life-or-death threats every day, and innovation is what helps them deter and defeat our shared enemies. Israel holds up its side of the alliance, and we will continue to collaborate and share what we learn so we both get stronger. This partnership will maintain safety for our countries and economic advances to create jobs. I remain proud to call our friends in Israel a trusted partner and ally.”
This marks Senator Scott’s seventh trip to Israel since his election as Governor of Florida in 2010; his recent travel itinerary also included Cyprus and Greece.
Scott champions fiscal responsibility as well as policies supporting families and small businesses; he served on active duty in the Navy after high school; he earned degrees from University of Missouri-Kansas City (business) and Southern Methodist University (law); he serves on several Senate committees including Armed Services; he was elected as Florida's senator; together with his wife Ann has raised two daughters—all according to, the official website.
